providers.selectedSource: Official Codex app-server account/rateLimits/read plus optional account/read (refreshToken: false)
providers.sourceStatusReason: The user approved the reviewed process boundary. Token Tank starts only the official stdio server, advertises no filesystem or terminal capability, and never reads or mutates Codex credentials.
providers.credentialPersistence: Codex-owned store; Token Tank does not read, copy, write, or rotate it
tokenTankIO: Launch an allowlisted codex app-server per native account source: explicit CODEX_HOME ~/.codex, and optional ~/.codex-secondary with -c cli_auth_credentials_store="file"
Exchange initialize, initialized, account/rateLimits/read, and optional account/read (refreshToken: false) JSONL over stdio
Read size-bounded responses, then terminate each child after the responses or exact timeout; keep quota data, freshness and failures independent per account source
externalPaths: ~/.codex (Codex-owned home; no credential file opens by Token Tank)
providers.liveValidation: Two independent native CODEX_HOME environments returned distinct ChatGPT account emails and successful general weekly rate limits on 2026-09-05. No GJC credential or usage dependency. Final application-candidate validation remains a separate gate.
providers.mutationRisk: The app-server owner may maintain its own credential; Token Tank sends no auth mutation method.
providers.releaseBlocker: Revalidate the owner session and sanitized shape through the final frozen candidate

providers.surface: Claude Code local session and weekly usage windows
providers.sourceStatusReason: Claude Code writes local five-hour, weekly, and scoped utilization that Orca already displays. Token Tank reads that cache in place, never presents organization Admin API usage as consumer quota, and never reads Claude credentials.
providers.credentialPersistence: Claude-owned ~/.claude.json; Token Tank does not persist, copy, write, or refresh credentials
tokenTankIO: Open only ~/.claude.json with the exact external-session capability
Expose cachedUsageUtilization limits and named windows under stable opaque IDs
Display optional oauthAccount.emailAddress from the same cache in memory only
providers.liveValidation: Current-host Claude Code cache exposed session, weekly_all, and weekly_scoped Fable utilization with source reset timestamps.
providers.mutationRisk: Read-only exact-path open. No credential copy, refresh, or Admin API fallback is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: Revalidate the local cache schema and exact owner path through the final frozen candidate

providers.sourceStatusReason: This is the CodexBar SuperGrok credits path: the Grok CLI owner session plus the documented CLI-proxy credits endpoint. Token Tank never copies or refreshes the token, never imports browser cookies, never uses grok agent stdio, and never calls the xAI Management prepaid-balance API.
providers.rejectedAlternative: The CodexBar-observed Grok Build ACP x.ai/billing extension returned JSON-RPC -32601 (method-not-found) on official Grok 1.0.13; browser-cookie, gRPC-web, and local-session-estimate fallbacks remain prohibited.
providers.credentialPersistence: Grok-owned ~/.grok/auth.json; Token Tank does not persist, copy, write, or refresh credentials
tokenTankIO: Open only ~/.grok/auth.json with the exact external-session capability
HTTPS GET https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing?format=credits with the ephemeral owner bearer
Expose published creditUsagePercent or the same-row onDemandUsed/onDemandCap ratio under the credits quota
Display only the selected auth entry's optional email in memory; never infer identity from another entry or token
providers.liveValidation: Current-host Grok CLI auth.json exists with an OIDC SuperGrok session; credits payload parsing is fixture-tested.
providers.mutationRisk: Read-only exact-path open. No credential copy, refresh, cookie import, or Management API fallback is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: Revalidate the owner session and sanitized CLI-proxy credits shape through the final frozen candidate

providers.surface: Cursor individual account usage summary and billing-cycle quota blocks
providers.selectedSource: Read-only Cursor.app state.vscdb session plus cursor.com/api/usage-summary
providers.sourceStatusReason: Cursor documents the usage surface but not the local session layout or usage-summary endpoint. Token Tank follows the current CodexBar behavior as a reference, reads the Cursor-owned SQLite value in place with immutable=1 and no persistence or refresh, and fails closed on expiry or schema drift.
providers.credentialPersistence: Cursor-owned state.vscdb; Token Tank does not persist, copy, write, or refresh the JWT
tokenTankIO: Open only Cursor/User/globalStorage/state.vscdb with O_NOFOLLOW, verify the opened descriptor identity, bind immutable=1 SQLite to that descriptor, and query only ItemTable cursorAuth/accessToken and cursorAuth/cachedEmail
Require a canonical token envelope, bounded allowed subject, and unexpired timestamp; use it only in an ephemeral owner-session cookie whose authority is decided by cursor.com/api/usage-summary
Expose individual and team usage blocks, plan breakdowns, and percentages independently with opaque identities
Display optional cachedEmail from the same SQLite read in memory only; absent or invalid email does not suppress usage
providers.liveValidation: Immutable exact-key read preserved all tracked main/WAL/SHM facts and the owner session returned the expected usage-summary root and individual plan/onDemand blocks; ordinary mode=ro was rejected after it changed SQLite metadata.
providers.mutationRisk: Immutable SQLite ignores active WAL state rather than touching shared-memory metadata; an older/expired checkpointed token fails closed. No browser import, token cache, copy, refresh, or external-store mutation is allowed.
providers.releaseBlocker: Revalidate the descriptor-bound immutable read, sanitized schema, and exact owner path through the final frozen candidate

providers.sourceStatusReason: This is the CodexBar Doubao path: the official arkcli CLI owns SSO and prints plan windows. Token Tank starts only the allowlisted arkcli executable with those literal arguments, never copies Volcengine credentials, and never signs OpenAPI requests.
providers.rejectedAlternative: App-owned AK/SK GetCodingPlanUsage remains fixture-tested history only and is not composed. Browser cookies and estimates remain prohibited.
providers.credentialPersistence: arkcli-owned SSO; Token Tank does not persist, copy, write, or refresh credentials
tokenTankIO: Launch one allowlisted arkcli executable candidate with the literal arguments usage plan --format json
Read one size-bounded JSON payload, then terminate the child after the response or exact timeout
Expose every plan window under stable opaque IDs; derive remaining/percentage only by exact same-row arithmetic
providers.liveValidation: Current-host arkcli exists; live usage plan currently fails closed on expired Volcengine SSO and asks for arkcli auth login.
providers.mutationRisk: The CLI owner may maintain its own credential; Token Tank sends no auth mutation method.
providers.releaseBlocker: Revalidate the owner session and sanitized arkcli JSON shape through the final frozen candidate
